analysis.investment_thesis: Exato is a tiny IT-enabled services play with strong ROE (28.2%) but decelerating revenue growth (56% → 9%), rising debt, and erratic cash flows — not the quality IT story India needs. At 35x P/E for a 338 Cr micro-cap with only 10 Cr PAT and zero FCF, the risk-reward is unfavourable.
key_strengths: ROE 28.2% and ROCE 26.5% — capital efficient at current scale
Operates in India's IT services tailwind with FY25 PAT doubling to 10 Cr
key_risks: Revenue growth collapsed from 56% (FY24) to 9% (FY25) — thesis breaking
Borrowings quadrupled from 6 Cr to 28 Cr in 2 years for an asset-light IT co
FCF swung 10 → -20 → 0 Cr; OCF negative in FY24 despite reported profits
red_flags: Rising leverage inconsistent with IT-services business model
Weak cash conversion — FY25 PAT 10 Cr but FCF zero
35x P/E on a single-digit-growth micro-cap with unproven track record (listed 2016, IPO-era)
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From my lens, India's IT sector offers decades of runway, but one must pick the right horse. Exato is sub-scale (124 Cr revenue, 10 Cr PAT) in the commoditised IT-enabled services space, not the high-margin product/SaaS bucket where multiples are earned. The ROE of 28% and FY25 profit doubling look attractive on paper, but revenue growth decelerated sharply from 56% to 9% — that is a yellow flag I don't ignore. Paying 35x earnings for that trajectory in a micro-cap with no moat is speculation, not investment.

The balance sheet also worries me — borrowings up from 6 Cr to 28 Cr while the business generated zero FCF in FY25 and burned 20 Cr in FY24. Good IT businesses throw off cash; this one is funding itself with debt and equity raises (reserves jumped from 27 Cr to 42 Cr). Promoter holding at 54.73% is adequate but not commanding. I'd wait for 2-3 more years of consistent execution, positive FCF, and deleveraging before paying this multiple. Avoid at current price.
